author: KERNAL Content Team
title: Feature Selection
subtitle: Removing irrelevant features to improve models

whyItExists.problem: Datasets often contain dozens or hundreds of features, many of which are irrelevant, redundant, or noisy. Including them increases overfitting, slows training, complicates the model, and makes it harder to interpret.
whyItExists.solution: Feature selection systematically identifies and removes features that don't contribute useful information, leaving only those that genuinely help predict the target.
whyItExists.whenToUse: When you have high-dimensional data (many features), when the model overfits despite regularisation, when you need a faster/simpler production model, or when stakeholders need to understand which factors drive predictions.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: When you have very few features already, or when using deep learning on images/text — the network learns its own feature selection internally.

explainModes.beginner: If you're trying to predict whether it will rain, features like 'humidity' and 'cloud cover' are very useful. Features like 'your lucky number' are useless. Feature selection is the process of throwing away the useless stuff so the model focuses on what matters.
explainModes.simple: Feature selection removes columns from the dataset that don't help predict the target. Some techniques rank features by statistical relationship with the target. Others train a model and check which features the model found important. You keep the top K.
explainModes.standard: Filter methods rank features by statistical criteria (F-statistic, mutual information). Wrapper methods (RFE) train the model iteratively, removing the least important feature each round. Embedded methods (Lasso) perform selection as part of training.
explainModes.technical: Filter methods are model-agnostic and fast but ignore feature interactions. Wrapper methods (RFE) capture interactions but are expensive. Embedded methods (Lasso, Random Forest importance) are the best compromise. Permutation importance is the most reliable post-hoc selection method.
explainModes.deepDive: Feature selection is a combinatorial search over 2^n subsets. Greedy wrapper methods (forward selection, backward elimination, RFE) approximate this. Stability selection applies Lasso to bootstrapped subsamples — features selected consistently across subsamples are robust. SHAP values provide theoretically grounded feature attribution.

content.text: Fewer, better features reduce overfitting, speed up training, and make models more interpretable. Including irrelevant or redundant features introduces noise and can actually hurt performance. The goal: keep only the features that genuinely help predict the target.

items: Reduces overfitting — fewer parameters to learn from noise
Speeds up training and prediction — less computation
Improves interpretability — easier to explain 10 features than 500
Reduces data collection costs — if 20 features are enough, don't measure 200

content.text: Filter methods rank features by their statistical relationship with the target — independently of any model. They are fast but can miss complex interactions between features.

content.code:
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, f_classif, mutual_info_classif
import pandas as pd

# F-statistic (ANOVA): tests linear relationship, good for numeric features
selector_f = SelectKBest(score_func=f_classif, k=10)
X_new_f = selector_f.fit_transform(X_train, y_train)
selected_mask_f = selector_f.get_support()
print('Selected by F-test:', list(X.columns[selected_mask_f]))

# Mutual information: captures non-linear relationships
selector_mi = SelectKBest(score_func=mutual_info_classif, k=10)
X_new_mi = selector_mi.fit_transform(X_train, y_train)
selected_mask_mi = selector_mi.get_support()
print('Selected by MI:', list(X.columns[selected_mask_mi]))

# View scores
scores = pd.Series(selector_mi.scores_, index=X.columns)
print(scores.sort_values(ascending=False).head(15))

content.text: RFE trains a model, removes the least important feature, then retrains — repeating until only the desired number of features remain. It captures feature interactions that filter methods miss.

content.code:
from sklearn.feature_selection import RFE, RFECV
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold

# Standard RFE: select exactly N features
rf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
rfe = RFE(estimator=rf, n_features_to_select=15, step=1)
rfe.fit(X_train, y_train)

selected = [feat for feat, sel in zip(X.columns, rfe.support_) if sel]
print(f'Selected {len(selected)} features:', selected)
print(f'Score with selected features: {rfe.score(X_test, y_test):.3f}')

# RFECV: automatically find the optimal number of features
rfecv = RFECV(
    estimator=RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42),
    cv=StratifiedKFold(5),
    scoring='f1',
    min_features_to_select=5
)
rfecv.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(f'Optimal number of features: {rfecv.n_features_}')

content.text: Permutation importance measures how much model performance drops when a feature's values are randomly shuffled. If shuffling a feature doesn't hurt performance, it was not useful. This works with any fitted model and is more reliable than tree-based feature importance.

content.code:
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Train the model first
model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, random_state=42)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Permutation importance on the test set
result = permutation_importance(
    model, X_test, y_test,
    n_repeats=10,          # shuffle each feature 10 times and average
    random_state=42,
    scoring='f1',
    n_jobs=-1
)

perm_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'feature': X.columns,
    'importance_mean': result.importances_mean,
    'importance_std': result.importances_std
}).sort_values('importance_mean', ascending=False)

print(perm_df.head(15))

# Remove features that hurt performance when shuffled (negative or near-zero importance)
useful_features = perm_df[perm_df['importance_mean'] > 0.001]['feature'].tolist()
print(f'Keeping {len(useful_features)} useful features')

from sklearn.linear_model import LassoCV
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import numpy as np

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_sc = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)

# LassoCV finds optimal alpha via CV and drives unimportant coefficients to zero
lasso = LassoCV(cv=5, random_state=42)
lasso.fit(X_train_sc, y_train)

selected_mask = lasso.coef_ != 0
selected_features = X.columns[selected_mask]
print(f'Lasso selected {selected_mask.sum()} / {len(X.columns)} features')
print(f'Selected: {list(selected_features)}')

content.text: Prefer permutation importance over tree-based feature importance (model.feature_importances_). Tree importance is biased towards high-cardinality features and can be misleading. Permutation importance is model-agnostic and evaluated on the test set.
Always do feature selection on the training set only. If you rank features by correlation with the target on the full dataset first, you've used test-set information — a form of data leakage.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE)?
options: To recursively add the most important features one at a time
To iteratively remove the least important feature until a target count is reached
To split data into folds for cross-validation
questions.explanation: RFE trains a model, identifies the least important feature, removes it, and repeats — until only the desired number of features remain. RFECV automates the selection of that number.

questions.question: Why is permutation importance more reliable than Random Forest's built-in feature importance?
options: Permutation importance is faster to compute
Built-in importance favours features with many unique values; permutation importance is unbiased
Permutation importance works only on the training set
questions.explanation: Random Forest's built-in importance is biased towards high-cardinality features because there are more possible splits. Permutation importance measures actual impact on test-set performance, which is unbiased.

questions.question: What is an advantage of filter methods over wrapper methods like RFE?
options: Filter methods are much faster since they don't require training a model
Filter methods always select the optimal subset
Filter methods work better for high-dimensional data
questions.explanation: Filter methods rank features by statistical criteria (F-test, mutual information) without training a model, making them much faster. The trade-off is they can miss interactions between features.

faq.q: Can feature importance from Random Forest be misleading?
faq.a: Yes. Random Forest's built-in feature importance (Gini importance) tends to favour high-cardinality features (many unique values) because there are more possible split points. Use permutation importance for a more reliable, unbiased estimate.

faq.q: How many features should I keep?
faq.a: Use RFECV to find the optimal number automatically, or look at the diminishing returns in the permutation importance ranking. As a rule of thumb, start with sqrt(n_features) and increase if the model underfits.

faq.q: Should I do feature selection before or after hyperparameter tuning?
faq.a: Ideally, feature selection and hyperparameter tuning should be done together (nested cross-validation). In practice, do feature selection first with a default model, then tune hyperparameters on the reduced feature set.

examples: Reducing 20,000 gene expression features to 50 predictive genes for a cancer classifier
Selecting 15 key features from 300 sensor readings for a predictive maintenance model
Using Lasso to identify which of 1,000 marketing attributes drive customer conversion
